- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.2) — model tends to ignore downside risk; add buffer to forecast lows.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted in early forecast windows — model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2 day lag correction for sentiment-driven reversals.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — model tends to overcorrect or over-forecast continuation; cap forecast peaks at 1.2x prior high or 1.5x recent 7-day average.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5x recent 14-day average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment > 0.7 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should trend upward; if sentiment < -0.3 for 3+ days, forecast should trend downward — model often misses this persistence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to over-optimism — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per 10-day horizon if sentiment is weak or volatile.
